title: Cache Preemption Poisoning Attacks on LLM-Based Log Parsers

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to introduce a new attack vector exploiting adaptive caching in LLM-based log parsers. None of the prior papers explicitly introduce or discuss an attack vector targeting adaptive caching in LLM-based log parsers. Papers [6], [7], [10], [12], [20], [21], [25], and [26] discuss cache-related attacks, but they focus on DNS cache poisoning, web cache pollution, or cache timing attacks, which are unrelated to adaptive caching in LLM-based log parsers. Paper [9] introduces adversarial attacks on log parsers but does not address adaptive caching mechanisms. Therefore, the purpose is **uncovered**.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves cache preemption poisoning, where crafted log lines front-load over-generalized templates to intercept later clean logs via prefix-tree matching. Paper [4] (LILAC) describes the use of prefix-tree caching in LLM-based log parsers but does not discuss poisoning or adversarial manipulation of the cache. Papers [6], [7], [10], [12], [20], [21], [25], and [26] discuss various cache-related attacks, but none involve prefix-tree matching or poisoning mechanisms specific to log parsing. Paper [9] introduces adversarial attacks on log parsers but does not involve cache poisoning or prefix-tree manipulation. Therefore, the mechanism is **uncovered**.

### Evaluation
The evaluation demonstrates the attack qualitatively on LILAC's prefix-tree cache as an exploitable surface created by the efficiency mechanism. Paper [4] (LILAC) uses prefix-tree caching for efficiency but does not evaluate it as an attack surface. Papers [6], [7], [10], [12], [20], [21], [25], and [26] evaluate cache-related attacks, but none use prefix-tree caching or LILAC's specific setup. Paper [9] evaluates adversarial attacks on log parsers but does not involve prefix-tree caching or qualitative demonstrations of cache poisoning. Therefore, the evaluation design is **uncovered**.

### Domain
The domain is the security of LLM-based log parsing. Papers [1], [2], [3], [4], [5], [8], [11], and [13] all address LLM-based log parsing, including its efficiency, accuracy, and security aspects. Paper [9] specifically discusses adversarial attacks on log parsers, which falls within the security domain of LLM-based log parsing. Therefore, the domain is **covered**.
